```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)


library("dplyr") # data cleaning and handling
library("modelsummary") # outputting results where needed
library(tidyr) 
library(broom)
library(purrr)
library(srvyr) # used for logit regressions with complex survey designs
library(svyVGAM) # used for PPO regressions with complex survey designs 
 
# Load project configuration
source(here::here("R", "load_config.R"))
cfg <- load_config()

# Construct input file path
input_2024 <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$output_file_2024_1year
)

input_2019 <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$output_file_2019_1year
)

input_means <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$outout_file_ACS_1year_means
)

input_dis <- file.path(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  cfg$IPUMS$output_file_ACS_1year_IncDis
)


## independent variables to be used in the regressions below.  This means you only
## need to update them here.

x_vector <- ("HHSize + ChildPresent + SeniorPresent + AGE + LF + SEX") 

stopifnot(file.exists(input_2019))
stopifnot(file.exists(input_2024))
stopifnot(file.exists(input_means))
stopifnot(file.exists(input_dis))

```

## load the 2024 data and run the model, using model summary to report the statistically significant coefficents. 
 
```{r}

ACS_1year_2024 <- read.csv(file.path(input_2024)) ## loads 2024 data

ACS_1year_means <-read.csv(file.path(input_means))

ACS_1year_dis <-read.csv(file.path(input_dis))

Weighted_IPUMS <-as_survey(ACS_1year_2024, id=CLUSTER,
                           weights=HHWT,
                           strata=STRATA,
                           nest=TRUE)

## This is to loop over the different logit models in R and produce 1 result for each

y_vector <-  names(ACS_1year_2024 %>% select(num_range("Inc", 1:14))) # vector of Inc to loop over


## the for loop using lapply, takes in the vector of Inc variables, combines
## the formula of x and y variables, then runs them through the svglm function
## saves the results in the models object.  
models <- lapply(y_vector, function(y) {
  
  logitformula <- reformulate(termlabels = x_vector, response = y)
  
  svyglm(logitformula, design = Weighted_IPUMS, family =  binomial (link = "logit"))
})

## adds the Inc# as the name of the lists stored in models, easier to call
## e.g. if you want the results for Inc1 you can call models$Inc1 

names(models) <- y_vector


# Extract significant coefficients (p < 0.05) per model
sig_coeffs_list <- map(models, ~ {
  tidy(.x) %>%
    filter(p.value < 0.05) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") # Optional: remove intercept
})

# View the resulting list
#print(sig_coeffs_list)

# Run new models using only the statistically significant varriables 
refitted_models <- map2(models, sig_coeffs_list, ~ {
  sig_terms <- .y$term
  
  # Handle cases where a model had 0 significant predictors (intercept-only)
  new_formula <- if (length(sig_terms) > 0) {
    reformulate(sig_terms, response = ".")
  } else {
    . ~ 1
  }
  
  update(.x, formula = new_formula)
})

#View the resulting models

#print(refitted_models)

# Generate predicted probabilities
pred_matrix <- sapply(refitted_models, function(mod) {
  predict(mod,
          newdata = ACS_1year_means,
          type = "response")
})

pred_bespoke_2024 <- as.data.frame(pred_matrix) %>%
  mutate(YEAR = ACS_1year_means$YEAR) %>%
  relocate(YEAR)
# Sum probabilities across income categories for each observation
rowSums(pred_matrix)
```

## Produce a table comparing the two models, showing all coefficients and relevant model comparison statistics 


```{r model-comparison, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
 

# Pair each original model next to its refitted model
paired_models <- map2(models, refitted_models, ~ list(Original = .x, Refitted = .y)) %>%
  flatten()

names(paired_models) <- paste0(
  rep(names(models), each = 2),
  c(" (Original)", " (Refitted)")
)

output_tex  <- file.path(
    cfg$paths$output_PDF_dir,
    cfg$Compare$pdf_bespoke
  )

# Render directly into the knitted R Markdown document
modelsummary(
  paired_models,
  stars = TRUE,
  gof_map = c("rmse", "aic", "bic", "adj.r.squared"),
  title = "Original vs. Significant-Only Models 2024",
  #output = output_tex
)
```

## Export the predictions to csv
```{r}


stopifnot(!is.null(cfg$paths$output_dir))

## export individual logit predictions 2024 data

# Create output directory if it does not exist
dir.create(
  cfg$paths$output_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

years <- c("2019", "2024")

## make a list of output matrices for bespoke logit models
pred_matrices <- list(
  `2019` = pred_bespoke_2019,
  `2024` = pred_bespoke_2024
)


## file list for export
bespoke_files <- list(
  `2019` = cfg$Predict$output_file_bespoke_2019_1year,
  `2024` = cfg$Predict$output_file_bespoke_2024_1year
)

# uses pred_matricies but any would work
for (yr in years) {
  
  print(yr)
  
  print(cfg$paths$output_dir)
  
  
  # create filepath for bespoke models
  output_bespoke <- file.path(
    cfg$paths$output_dir,
    bespoke_files[[yr]]
  )

 
 # write csv for bespoke models
  write.csv(
    pred_matrices[[yr]],
    output_bespoke,
    row.names = FALSE
  )


 
}

  
 #clean up the memory
rm(list = ls())


```
